panels.title: PostgreSQL process CPU
panels.description: Sampled PostgreSQL processes; 100% is one CPU core. Very short-lived processes may be missed.

panels.title: Hub task rows
panels.description: PostgreSQL's estimated live and dead row counts; dead rows are not necessarily reclaimable immediately.

panels.title: Table block access rate
panels.description: PostgreSQL table and index block hits and reads by source.

panels.title: Sequential rows read / sec by table
panels.description: Rows read by sequential scans, including rows later rejected by filters. PostgreSQL table statistics, one-minute rate.

panels.title: Index rows fetched / sec by table
panels.description: Live table rows fetched by index scans; not index entries examined or rows from index-only scans.

options.content: Top statements show estimated execution time during the selected time range, sampled every 15 seconds. Execution time includes waits and concurrent calls; it is not CPU time. New or evicted statements and collection gaps can make totals incomplete. At least two samples are required. Query text is truncated to 500 characters. I/O counts are PostgreSQL shared and temporary blocks read or written, not necessarily physical disk I/O.

panels.title: Statistics reset (all databases)
panels.description: pg_stat_statements reset time applies across databases. Individual entries can also be reset or evicted.

targets.rawSql: SELECT stats_reset AS "Statistics reset" FROM pg_stat_statements_info

panels.title: Top queries by execution time in selected range
panels.description: Estimated execution milliseconds in the selected range, ranked by total execution time. Counters are sampled every 15 seconds and require at least two samples; newly observed or evicted statements may be undercounted.

panels.title: Top queries by blocks read and written in selected range
panels.description: Ranked by shared and temporary blocks read and written. PostgreSQL block counts are buffer activity, not necessarily physical disk I/O. Sampled every 15 seconds; counter resets, newly observed or evicted statements, and collection gaps can make estimates incomplete. At least two samples are required.
